references.text: The sick man at the Pool of Bethesda describes his own helplessness – he had no one to help him into the water. This elaborates on the situation of the sick lying in the colonnades ([ref:Joh 5:7|John 5:7]).
Blind, paralyzed, and other sick people sought healing. In [ref:Matt 9:2|Matthew 9:2], a paralyzed man is brought to Jesus for healing, paralleling the paralyzed at the Pool of Bethesda.
Large crowds of sick – paralyzed, blind, mute, and crippled – were brought to Jesus for healing, which recalls the crowd of sick lying at Bethesda ([ref:Matt 15:30-31|Matthew 15:30-31]).
Blind and lame people came to Jesus in the temple, and he healed them. These categories of the sick – blind and lame – correspond to those mentioned in [ref:Matt 21:14|Matthew 21:14].

Isaiah's prophecy that the eyes of the blind will be opened and the legs of the paralyzed will leap – a messianic expectation that forms the background for the blind and lame at Bethesda who waited for healing ([ref:Jes 35:5-6|Isaiah 35:5-6]).
A man who had been paralyzed from birth was placed at the temple gate to beg – a parallel to the sick lying in the colonnades at Bethesda ([ref:Apg 3:2|Acts 3:2]).

People carried their sick out into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, so that Peter's shadow might fall on them. This recalls the crowd of sick at Bethesda who waited for healing ([ref:Apg 5:15-16|Acts 5:15-16]).
One of the sick lying there had been ill for thirty-eight years, illustrating the severity of the condition of those described in verse 3 ([ref:Joh 5:5|John 5:5]).
